(7) Static lock analysis: the attribution command takes the target request FOR UPDATE, then the fence FOR UPDATE, then source, policy and grant FOR SHARE. Every predecessor path uses the same request-before-fence order: event append, reservation, create context, create result, identity binding, settlement and eligibility. No path takes a request after the fence. I found no deadlock on the canonical paths. A grant, policy or source revoked mid-command is refused, because the locked FOR SHARE recheck re-evaluates the row after the revoker commits. Duplicate commits serialize on the request lock, and journal_id is unique. The classifier reads attributions while holding the fence.

The real gap is order dependence. A fully specified event for the same payment that arrives before the attribution is classified as a permanent conflict, and the candidate can never attribute it. The source then stays quarantined, so the unrelated-order relief never happens. This ordering is untested and the records do not mention it.
